title: The dual-number projection square is cartesian
statement: Let $X,Y$ be arbitrary schemes [def-pc-scheme] and $f:X\to Y$ any morphism. Write $p_X:X[\epsilon]\to X$ and $p_Y:Y[\epsilon]\to Y$ for the projections of the dual-number thickenings [def-sc-dual-numbers], and $f[\epsilon]$ for the induced morphism. The square with top map $p_X$, left map $f[\epsilon]$, right map $f$ and bottom map $p_Y$ is cartesian: $\operatorname{IsPullback}(p_X,f[\epsilon],f,p_Y)$. There are no finiteness, affineness, smoothness, or characteristic hypotheses.

source.place: Scheme.isPullback_dualNumbersProj and its explicit square-zero evaluation construction, lines 46-243

proof.text: For a scheme T and a square-zero global section t, construct T to T[epsilon] on each open by a+epsilon b mapping to a+tb, with identity base map. This is a ring homomorphism because t squared is zero and commutes with restrictions. It is local on stalks because a nilpotent perturbation preserves invertibility. Its composite with the projection is the identity. These are the proved evalSqZero, liftSqZero, liftSqZero_appLE and liftSqZero_comp_proj helpers in the source.

For h:T to Y[epsilon], let t=h-sharp(epsilon), which is square-zero. On each open decompose a dual number into inl(a)+inl(b)*inr(1). Naturality identifies the restriction of t with the image of inr(1), so h factors as the evaluation morphism followed by (h composed with p_Y)[epsilon]. The source proves this as eq_liftSqZero_comp_dualNumbers.

Given a commuting cone a:T to X and b:T to Y[epsilon], use evaluation at b-sharp(epsilon) followed by a[epsilon]. The preceding factorization and functoriality give both projection equations. For any other lift, its X projection is a and its epsilon image is determined by b because f[epsilon] preserves epsilon. The factorization therefore proves equality of the lifts. Apply the pullback-cone universal property; the source implements these three checks in isPullback_dualNumbersProj.
